one_sentence: The delayed-choice quantum eraser and the Cross are the same mathematical event at different scales, with retrocausality mapping to atonement.
executive_summary: This document argues that the delayed-choice quantum eraser (Scully & Druhl 1982, Kim et al. 1999) and the Christian doctrine of the Cross are structurally isomorphic. The core claim is that a future measurement choice retroactively determines past behavior in the quantum eraser, mirroring how the Cross, though occurring in 33 AD, is an eternal event (Revelation 13:8) that retroactively determines the meaning of history. The key evidence includes the experimentally confirmed retrocausal correlations in the quantum eraser and scriptural references to the Lamb slain before the foundation of the world. The conclusion is that the atonement is not a reactive Plan B but a retrocausal event from the eternal frame, with four historical atonement theories (Penal Substitution, Christus Victor, Moral Influence, Recapitulation) being projections of this single event. The isomorphism passes four separator tests (structural preservation, non-arbitrariness, constraint, bidirectionality), establishing it as a Level 3 structural isomorphism.
short_summary: This document is a formal isomorphism paper mapping the delayed-choice quantum eraser to the Christian atonement. The core structural claim is that a future measurement choice retroactively determines past behavior in both domains, with the Cross being an eternal event that projects into time. Key evidence includes the experimentally confirmed Kim et al. 1999 quantum eraser results and scriptural references to the Lamb slain before the foundation of the world (Revelation 13:8). This matters because it provides a rigorous mathematical framework for understanding atonement as retrocausal, unifying four historical theories and establishing a bidirectional predictive relationship between physics and theology.
